- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤ 0.25), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to match subdued market sentiment.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes in price — especially in 30-day horizon — leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor if price rises > 5% from prior 7-day average.  
- In cases where true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model often fails to anticipate it; add a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion buffer in forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.5–1.0 over 3+ days), model tends to lag behind true price; adjust forecast to be 1–2% ahead of historical trend.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period volatility — especially after sentiment shifts — so add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment turns bullish within last 5 days.
